page: Amazon Web Services m8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz and a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 768 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a 75 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. The server's memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier read and write bandwidth for large uncached blocks. In database and key-value store benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results, including 262.57 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and top-tier PassMark database operations.

While multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics consistently rank in the top 10%, single-core performance presents a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the middle 50% average. For LLM inference, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds for small and medium models, but text generation for small models drops to the middle 50% average. Given the high-density compute, large local NVMe storage, and 75 Gbps network baseline, this bare-metal instance is configured for database hosting, large-scale software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
